proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) ≤ x. Subtracting floor(x) from both sides gives x - floor(x) ≥ 0. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Use the defining property floor(x) ≤ x, then subtract floor(x) to obtain x - floor(x) ≥ 0 for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly uses the defining property of floor(x) <= x and derives x - floor(x) >= 0 for an arbitrary real x. This exactly matches the lemma statement and is complete.
